title: Сумка с выкупом и прогулка с улитками  (The Ransom Bag and Walking the Snails)

segments.t: At home, Nastya's father stuffs a bag with cash for the ransom drop while his wife pleads with him not to take a gun and insists Kostya ride along to keep him from doing anything reckless. Back at the restaurant, Chef Barinov catches Max sneaking in through the back door.
Больше берите, его же там все равно много.
Мне бармены в машине не нужны.
Пусть едет, иначе ты там глупости натворишь.
Right, let's take their exchange slowly and unpack the Russian.
Больше берите, его же там все равно много.
'Take more of it, there is plenty of it in there anyway.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'more' and finishing on 'much'.
'Just in case.' Dmitry brings out the contrast between 'on' and 'every' in a few short words.
'Do not even think about bringing a weapon.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'not' and finishing on 'weapons'. Dmitry answers right away.
'I am not going to shoot anyone.' The meaning hinges on 'I' working together with 'will' in spoken Russian.
'Galya, do not worry.' The meaning hinges on 'Galya' working together with 'worry' in spoken Russian.
'You are scaring me already.' Dmitry addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'are scaring'. Vika answers right away.
'We are going to the police immediately.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'immediately' before landing on 'police'.
'I will handle this myself.' Dmitry brings out the contrast between 'himself' and 'will sort out' in a few short words.
Мне бармены в машине не нужны.
'I do not need any bartenders in my car.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'for me' and finishing on 'needed'. Dmitry answers right away.
'I am coming with you.' In Russian, the idea of 'I' flows naturally into 'with you' without extra filler words.
Пусть едет, иначе ты там глупости натворишь.
'Let him come along, otherwise you will do something foolish out there.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'let' before landing on 'to do'.
'I just went out for a smoke.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'I' and finishing on 'went'. Vika answers right away.

'And took the snails out for a walk at the same time?' Vika raises the pitch on 'to walk' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Now let's listen to the entire scene again without interruption.
Больше берите, его же там все равно много.
Мне бармены в машине не нужны.
Пусть едет, иначе ты там глупости натворишь.
